artworks.title: Latinus Offering his Daughter Lavinia to Aeneas in Matrimony
artworks.description: Tiepolo stages King Latinus as the host who yields Lavinia to the Trojan stranger — the oracle-bound father of Latium in Aeneid VII. Baroque gesture makes the Latin king the hinge between welcome and the war Alecto will kindle.

artworks.title: Aeneas before Latinus
artworks.description: Bol’s Rijksmuseum canvas (SK-A-614) shows Aeneas received at Latinus’ court — embassy, gifts, and the king who must weigh an oracle against Turnus’ claim. Dutch classicism keeps Latinus the seated authority of Latium’s first contact with Troy.

artworks.title: Alecto Rousing Latinus Against Aeneas
artworks.description: LACMA print of Alecto poisoning Latinus’ house against the Trojans — Virgil’s Fury at work on the Latin king. The image names Latinus as the mortal whose court becomes the fuse of the Italian war.

artworks.title: King Latinus Predicts Aeneas' Arrival in Latium
artworks.description: A Carracci-school scene of Latinus as prophetic host — the king who reads the omen of the foreign son-in-law. Italian disegno keeps him the Latian ruler of the Aeneid’s second half, not Hesiod’s Circean Latinus.

films.title: The Avenger
films.description: Peplum Aeneid: Latinus’ Latium, Lavinia’s hand, and the war that follows Aeneas ashore.

popCulture.title: Aeneid VII
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Virgil’s Latinus — son of Faunus, king of the Latins — welcomes Aeneas and offers Lavinia until Juno’s Fury turns Latium to war.
